deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck's combinatorial map ('carte') is encoded in its usual way as a set of flags F, i.e. the triangles of the barycentric subdivision. Three fixed-point-free involutions act on F: sigma0 changes the vertex, sigma1 changes the edge, and sigma2 changes the face. The only relation is that sigma0 and sigma2 commute; the corner where an edge meets a face side is a right angle. The rotation sigma0 sigma1 turns the flags inside a face, and sigma1 sigma2 turns them around a vertex.

Claim on the page. Suppose every vertex and every face has even degree. Then a face of degree 2m carries the half-turn sigma_f = (sigma0 sigma1)^m. Its dihedral group has order 4m, and the half-turn is the central element of that group. Likewise a vertex of degree 2n carries sigma_s = (sigma1 sigma2)^n.
- Both are fixed-point-free involutions.
- sigma_f commutes with sigma0 and sigma1, because conjugation inverts the rotation and the half-turn is its own inverse.
- sigma_s commutes with sigma1 and sigma2.
- sigma2 commutes with sigma0.
So the cyclic sequence (sigma0, sigma_f, sigma1, sigma_s, sigma2, back to sigma0) consists of five involutions in which each consecutive pair commutes. This is what '2 a 2 commutantes' means here, and it is literally true.

Geometric meaning. Grothendieck reads such a cyclic sequence as a 'pentagonal map'. The sketches show how: the flag triangle, with sides sigma0, sigma1, sigma2, has its face-centre corner cut off by a side labelled sigma_f and its vertex corner cut off by a side labelled sigma_s. The triangle becomes a pentagon with sides sigma0, sigma_f, sigma1, sigma_s, sigma2 in cyclic order. Every corner of this pentagon is a right angle: two consecutive involutions commute, so each vertex of the new tiling is surrounded by 4 chambers. This is the sense of 'sommets d'ordre deux'. Note that sigma0 and sigma1 no longer satisfy any relation as generators. The structure is therefore an action of the right-angled pentagon Coxeter group, which is a hyperbolic reflection group, in place of the cartographic group.

The visualisation Grothendieck says he lacks ('Je n'arrive pas bien a visualiser cette derniere carte'). The realisation is obtained by gluing right-angled pentagons. Across a sigma_f side, a flag is glued to its antipode in the same face. So around each face the truncated corners form a circle of 4m segments, and this circle is closed up by the antipodal identification. That means a small disc is removed and its boundary identified antipodally, i.e. a cross-cap, which is the real blow-up of the face centre. The same happens at each vertex.
- The pentagonal map is thus the original map on the surface X# (V+F) RP^2: the real blow-up of X at all vertices and face centres.
- Euler characteristic check. With N = 4E flags, the tiling has N pentagons, 5N/2 edges and 5N/4 vertices. So chi = 5N/4 - 5N/2 + N = -N/4 = -E. This equals (V - E + F) - V - F, which is what the cross-cap description predicts.

This fits the previous page, which discusses 'antipodique' identifications, superposingular lines and the sign sigma^nu picked up by parallel transport.

Right margin. There are tentative alternative labellings (sigma_s, sigma_a, sigma_r, sigma_vert, and 'a f s' on an orange line) with a fan of lines. These appear to be attempts to draw the configuration along a 'pseudo-line', in the spirit of the dossier on systems of pseudo-lines.
errors: No mathematical error. The commutation claim holds, but only between cyclically consecutive involutions. Non-consecutive ones (for example sigma0 and sigma1) do not commute in general, so '2 a 2 commutantes' must be read as 'consecutive ones commute'.

Implicit hypothesis: the half-turns are fixed-point-free involutions only if the degree is even, as stated. For odd degree the dihedral group has trivial centre and the construction fails, so the parity hypothesis is necessary.

ideas.what: Encoding of a map by three involutions sigma0, sigma1, sigma2 on flags, with sigma0 commuting with sigma2.
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / flag-graph (monodromy) description of maps

ideas.what: For a map with all vertex and face degrees even, the central half-turns sigma_f = (sigma0 sigma1)^m and sigma_s = (sigma1 sigma2)^n, which together with sigma0, sigma1, sigma2 form a cyclic 5-chain of involutions with consecutive pairs commuting.
ideas.modern_name: Action of the right-angled pentagon Coxeter group on flags; a derived 'pentagonal map' (a map operation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related to map operations (Wilson's operators, Petrie duals) but this specific construction is not known to me

ideas.what: Interpretation of n-cyclic chains of consecutively commuting involutions as 'n-gonal maps' (tilings by right-angled n-gons with 4-valent vertices).
ideas.modern_name: Right-angled Coxeter group actions / generalized maps

missed.claim: The pentagonal map attached to an even-even map is not visualised by Grothendieck. It can be identified as the original map on the surface obtained by real-blowing-up (inserting a cross-cap at) every vertex and every face centre; the Euler characteristic becomes -E. This links the cartographic group of even maps to the right-angled pentagon reflection group.
missed.quote: donc a une carte pentagonale ... Je n'arrive pas bien a visualiser cette derniere carte, en termes de la carte initiale....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a functorial operation from even dessins/maps to actions of a hyperbolic right-angled Coxeter group, with a clear topological meaning (real blow-up). This could interest people classifying map operations and their monodromy groups. It also connects with Grothendieck's pseudo-line and 'antipodal transport' considerations on the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is elementary but neat. A cyclic pentagon of commuting involutions extracted from an even map, giving a right-angled-pentagon structure, is not a standard named map operation as far as I know. Grothendieck leaves it unvisualised, and the real-blow-up interpretation is not hard. Its interest is modest.
transcription_corrections: 'pentagonale fondiere[?]' is uncertain in the image; it may be 'pentagonale' followed by an unclear word. The word 'fondiere' is doubtful.
'd'ordre deux en fait[?]' could also read 'deux en position'; the meaning is that all vertices have order (dihedral type) 2, i.e. 4 chambers meet.
The first line in the image shows dotted sigmas with a starred f: sigma0, sigma_f*, sigma1, sigma_s (overwritten, possibly s or 3), sigma2, followed by a scribble.
Right margin labels read sigma_s, sigma_a, sigma_r with sigma_vert below, and 'a f s' on the orange curve.
